conflicts.quote: Re-running the retained 2026-08-11 paired slice reproduces the deep dive's published figures to their published precision: composite AUC 0.467 and lift@top10 0.17, structure-event AUC 0.932, SPY Pearson +0.51, QQQ Pearson −0.31, SPY lift 1.43, QQQ lift 0.56.
conflicts.why: The word "retained" is the problem, and it is a dated problem. The raw structure diary is a per-symbol ring buffer, not an archive: `STRUCTURE_HISTORY_MAX = 576` and `STRUCTURE_HISTORY_MIN_INTERVAL_SECS = 300.0` (`store.rs:29-31`), enforced in memory by `merge_structure_sample` (`store.rs:153-170`) and in Postgres by the ring prune at `pg_scan.rs:468-490`. The 2026-08-11 slice itself gives the arithmetic: 221 paired rows / 3 symbols over a 6h43m window is ~74 samples per symbol per session, so 576 holds ~7-8 sessions per symbol. The slice is retrievable TODAY (its samples are from 2026-08-10, one session back). It will be evicted roughly seven trading sessions from now, at which point an AC-C4 test that reads the live diary goes red on a calendar date rather than on a code change — the worst failure mode a regression test can have. Separately, AC-C4 asks for per-symbol Pearson figures: `pearson()` exists (`score_lab.rs:488`) and is already reported pooled, but my R1 §7 cell content listed only AUC / precision / recall / lift / calibration and omitted correlation entirely. That omission is mine and I withdraw it — per-symbol Pearson is exactly the SPY +0.51 / QQQ −0.31 inversion the BRIEF names as the motivating hand-computed finding, so it must be a cell field, not a hand computation.
conflicts.proposal: Two changes, both cheap, both this week. (1) Freeze the slice now: commit the 2026-08-10/11 paired inputs (the `StructureSample` set and the `StructureOutcome` set, as fixture JSON under the test tree) before the ring evicts them, and write AC-C4 against that fixture. Restate AC-C4 as "re-running the committed 2026-08-11 fixture slice reproduces..." — a fixture test is deterministic, survives retention, and satisfies AC-C6 (two runs over identical inputs produce identical figures) at the same time. This converts PM's Open product decision #2 from a decision into a deadline. (2) Add `pearson_vs_abs_move` and `pearson_vs_ret_simple` to the per-cell content in my §7 so every candidate × group carries its correlation alongside its ranking metrics, and the per-symbol inversion is a field.

conflicts.quote: The standing verdict is **derived from the run's window/sample counts**, not a constant: a run below the session bar renders `BELOW BAR`/`DEGENERATE`, a run meeting it does not
conflicts.why: The clause "a run meeting it does not" describes a branch that no single run can reach, for a structural reason rather than a data-thinness reason. UX's own bar text is "sustained across >= N sessions spanning >= M calendar weeks". A single run's evidence is bounded by the ring buffer above: ~7-8 sessions per symbol maximum, which is under two calendar weeks even when completely full. So for any M >= 2 the `AT BAR` verdict is unreachable by construction, forever, from one run. PM's scope agrees and closes the other door: "Cross-run aggregation, trend lines, or week-over-week roll-up inside the tool" is Out, and the multi-week roll-up is Future-dated. A verdict vocabulary containing a state the code can never emit is a dead branch that UX-2 is written as a `test` against — the test can only ever assert the `BELOW BAR` half, so it does not test derivation at all, and the first person to read `BELOW BAR` forty weeks running concludes the block is the constant hedge UX-2 exists to prevent. This is not an argument against derivation; it is an argument that the quantity being derived must be one a run can know.
conflicts.proposal: Derive the standing from what one run genuinely knows, and make the unreachability explicit rather than latent. Concretely: (a) the run computes `sessions_counted` (distinct `session_date_et`, which `outcomes.rs:40` already carries) and `span_calendar_days` from first/last `as_of`, and the verdict is a pure function of those two against N and M; (b) for v1 the reachable vocabulary is `BELOW BAR` / `INSUFFICIENT — cannot evaluate` / `DEGENERATE — single session` / `DEGENERATE — single symbol`, and `AT BAR` is declared unreachable-from-one-run in the artifact itself — e.g. a `bar_evaluable_from_single_run: false` field with the retention ceiling (`STRUCTURE_HISTORY_MAX` in sessions) as its stated reason, so the reader learns the bar needs the cross-run roll-up PM future-dated; (c) UX-2's test then asserts the verdict *changes* across two fixtures (1 session vs 5 sessions -> `DEGENERATE — single session` vs `BELOW BAR`), which actually falsifies a hardcoded string. If the owner wants `AT BAR` reachable at all, that is a retention change (raising `STRUCTURE_HISTORY_MAX`) or the multi-week roll-up — both out of this feature's scope per my §12.4, and neither is mine to decide.

conflicts.quote: For each candidate, the pooled sample count equals the sum of its per-symbol counts plus its counted exclusions — the arithmetic reconciles in the printed output.
conflicts.why: This identity is false under its natural reading and will be encoded as a failing or wrongly-passing test. Let P be the paired rows in the slice, P_s the paired rows for symbol s (so sum of P_s = P), and for a candidate c let used_s + excluded_s = P_s. Then pooled used U = sum of used_s and pooled excluded E = sum of excluded_s, and the true identities are U = sum(used_s) and U + E = P. "Pooled count = sum of per-symbol counts PLUS exclusions" double-counts E: it is only true if the left-hand side means the paired total P rather than the candidate's pooled n, which is not what "its pooled sample count" reads as. A test written from this sentence either passes only when E = 0 (i.e. never once a candidate has a real exclusion, which is the case AC-D3 exists for) or is quietly rewritten by whoever hits it. UX-7 has the neighbouring version of the same slip — "used + excluded = paired rows" is true only when the row's scope is the whole slice; for a per-symbol row the right-hand side is that symbol's paired rows, not the pooled total.
conflicts.proposal: Split it into the two identities that are separately true and separately checkable, both computed from the same `excluded_by_reason` map in my §4: (1) COMPOSITION — for every candidate, the pooled used count equals the sum of its per-symbol used counts, and the pooled exclusion count equals the sum of the per-symbol exclusion counts, reason by reason; (2) CLOSURE — within any single scope (pooled, or one symbol), used + total excluded = that scope's paired row count. Stating them separately is what makes the arithmetic actually reconcile in print, and (1) is the stronger criterion because it is the one that catches a symbol silently dropped from the per-symbol section.

conflicts.quote: Computed set exists but is below the reporting floor; the value is **withheld, not shown small**
conflicts.why: This directly contradicts PM, who requires the opposite for the same cell. PM's state table gives "computed, under-powered" as "a value, with its n, marked as below the stated minimum", whose forbidden rendering is "a bare value" — i.e. the value IS shown, just never bare. PM's Open product decision #1 makes it explicit: the floor is "printed in the report, marked but never suppressed — a research tool must show thin numbers, it just must not show them bare". UX withholds; PM shows-with-a-marker. Both cannot hold, and the difference is not cosmetic: it decides whether the number exists in the artifact at all, which is my lane. My own R1 §7 sided with UX by making `InsufficientN { n, floor }` a `CellState` variant that carries no metric — I withdraw that shape regardless of how this is settled, because it destroys information at the data layer to serve a rendering preference, and it makes AC-C4/AC-C5 reproduction impossible for any thin cell. There is also a live instance: the 47-57 calibration bin UX cites is exactly the kind of cell whose value the deep dive quoted.
conflicts.proposal: Separate the data question from the rendering question, which lets the human settle only the part that is genuinely theirs. Data (mine, and I will build it either way): every cell that has >= 1 eligible row computes and CARRIES its metric values in the artifact, plus `n_eligible`, `floor_in_force`, and a boolean `under_powered` derived by the stated rule. Nothing is withheld from the file — a withheld artifact value cannot be reproduced, diffed week-over-week, or fed to the future roll-up. Rendering (UX's, and the thing the owner decides): whether the terminal/table shows `0.47 (n=4, below floor 30)` per PM or `too few (n=4, floor 30)` per UX. I have no stake in which literal prints; I have a hard stake in the artifact never being the place the number disappears. Note that if the owner picks UX's withholding for the console, UX-5's contrast test still works and PM's AC-G3 marker still prints — only the digits differ.

conflicts.quote: For the same slice and horizon, the composite score's pooled figures match what the pre-feature lab reported for that slice — the weekly series is not silently rebased.
conflicts.why: "Figures" is unqualified, and one family of figures cannot match under my §9. The shipped `calibration_curve` uses equal-width bins over [min, max] of the scalar. Equal-width is defensible for a bounded 0-100 score and is useless for `abs(net_gex)/vol_scalar`, which is heavy-tailed and spans orders of magnitude across symbols — it would put nearly every row in bin 1 and a single row in bin 5. My position is quantile (quintile) bins, one binning rule for every candidate, because a per-candidate binning rule makes the calibration column non-comparable across rows of the same table. That choice necessarily changes `opportunity_score`'s calibration table relative to the 2026-08-11 run: same rows, same labels, different bin edges, different per-bin counts. So AC-C5 as written is unmeetable, and the failure is silent in the direction that matters — someone will read "pooled figures match" as satisfied because the AUC matched, and the calibration change ships undeclared. The ranking metrics (base rate, AUC, precision@top10, lift@top10) DO match exactly, and my §11 parity oracle asserts that against `evaluate_baseline` retained as a test-only oracle.
conflicts.proposal: Scope AC-C5 to the metrics that are definitionally stable, and let PM's own AC-P4 carry the rest: "For the same slice and horizon, the composite score's pooled base rate, AUC, precision@top10 and lift@top10 match what the pre-feature lab reported for that slice. Calibration bin edges change with the new binning rule; the change is declared by a bump of the report version marker, and the pre-feature and post-feature values are both recorded in the parity test." This keeps PM's real requirement — the weekly series is not silently rebased — while making the one rebasing that does happen loud instead of undetectable. If PM would rather keep byte-identical calibration, the alternative is per-candidate binning rules, which I am arguing against on comparability grounds and would want the owner to see as the trade.

conflicts.quote: Re-running the retained 2026-08-11 paired slice reproduces the deep dive's published figures to their published precision: composite AUC 0.467 and lift@top10 0.17, structure-event AUC 0.932, SPY Pearson +0.51, QQQ Pearson −0.31, SPY lift 1.43, QQQ lift 0.56.
conflicts.why: I am withdrawing my own AC-C4; three separate findings kill it. (1) The architect verified the raw diary is a ring buffer — `STRUCTURE_HISTORY_MAX = 576`, 300s thinning, Postgres pruned to the same cap, roughly seven sessions per symbol — so the word 'retained' is false: those rows will be evicted well before this feature is built. (2) Architect §6 computes the `large_abs_move` threshold once per (horizon, slice) over the full paired set instead of per group, which moves the per-symbol base rates that the deep dive's hand-paired SPY 1.43 / QQQ 0.56 lifts were computed against — those two figures were never produced by a tool, so demanding a tool reproduce them to published precision is demanding it reproduce a hand computation of unknown scoping. (3) The two Pearson figures are not in the architect's §7 cell content at all. An AC that cannot be met by the design it governs is not a strong AC, it is a build-time argument.
conflicts.proposal: Split AC-C4 into two smaller, meetable criteria. (a) Continuity: the 2026-08-11 paired slice is pinned NOW as a committed fixture (a samples file plus an outcomes file, read via the file input path, never the live diary), and a run over that fixture reports the pooled composite figures the pre-feature lab reported for it — AUC 0.467 and lift@top10 0.17 — asserted against the parity oracle. (b) Inversion: on that same fixture, the SPY and QQQ cells for the composite candidate report opposite-signed association with the continuous outcome, asserted as a sign-and-ordering claim rather than to two decimals — and only if a correlation field exists per cell (see asks). If the slice cannot be pinned before eviction, (a) falls back to a constructed fixture and the reproduction claim is gone; I would rather lose the claim than keep an AC nobody can run.

conflicts.quote: Any cell below the report's stated minimum sample count carries the under-powered marker, and the minimum in force is printed in the run.
conflicts.why: My own AC-G3 says too little in light of the architect's evidence-weight finding. A floor expressed only in samples certifies the 2026-08-11 slice — 221 rows from one 7-hour window at a 5-minute cadence — as fully powered, because 221 clears any row floor I would set. The rows are massively autocorrelated; the true weight is one session. So the marker my no-mandate guards depend on would be absent on exactly the slice that motivated the guards. That is the failure mode I claim to design against, sitting in my own criterion.
conflicts.proposal: Restate AC-G3 with two floors, not one: every cell prints `n_rows` AND its distinct-session count, and carries the under-powered marker when it falls below EITHER the row floor or the session floor; a cell drawn from a single session carries the single-session marker regardless of row count. The numbers stay an owner decision, carried forward from my R1 open decisions — my recommendation is 30 rows per cell and a session floor of 2 for the marker (with the trust bar itself set much higher, see the UX-2 conflict).

conflicts.quote: v1 set — six candidates, three families, all derivable from captured fields:
conflicts.why: Five of the six I accept, including the one that was not in my scope list: `net_gex_abs_raw` is a genuine control, and without it a strong vol-norm row cannot be attributed to the normalization rather than to GEX magnitude — my own false-mandate risk argues for it, so I am not treating the BRIEF's three families as a scope fence. `net_gex_vol_norm_signed` is different in kind. It is not a control, it is a new directional hypothesis, and it is scored mostly against magnitude labels (`large_abs_move`, `structure_event`) where a signed candidate is near chance by construction. Its most likely output is an AUC near 0.50 that reads to the operator as 'vol-normalized GEX ranks at chance' while having tested something else entirely — a wrong-reading cell is worse than an absent one. It also adds twelve of the seventy-two cells on a report whose legibility collapse is one of my named risks, and the BRIEF's own invariant watch frames vol-norm GEX as a magnitude read.
conflicts.proposal: v1 is five candidates: `opportunity_score`, `net_gex_vol_norm_abs`, `net_gex_abs_raw` (control, paired eligibility as the architect specifies), `proximity_to_flip`, `proximity_to_nearer_wall`. If `net_gex_vol_norm_signed` stays, it is reported against the direction label only, where a signed scalar is a meaningful hypothesis, and is labelled a direction hypothesis rather than a magnitude read. Otherwise it is future-dated alongside `iv_hv_ratio` extremity. This is an owner call because it is a scope-versus-legibility trade on what the operator reads every week, not a feasibility question.

conflicts.quote: Computed set exists but is below the reporting floor; the value is **withheld, not shown small**
conflicts.why: This contradicts my R1 state table directly, where the under-powered state is 'a value, with its n, marked as below the stated minimum' and must not be shown as a bare value — marked, never suppressed. Withholding trades one collapse for another: a withheld cell and an uncomputable cell both render as 'no number here', which is the `[absent-is-not-none]` failure at the other end of the same axis. On this evidence base most cells will be thin for months; a rule that suppresses thin values means the operator sees almost no numbers at all, cannot watch a figure move week over week, and loses the only thing a research tool is for. The danger of a thin number is that it is quoted bare, and the fix for that is the marker plus the session count, not deletion.
conflicts.proposal: `too few` shows the value AND the marker in one literal — e.g. `0.61 (n=4, below floor 30 — under-powered)` — so it is textually distinct from `no input (...)`, from an above-floor value, and from a blank, in a plain-text paste with no surrounding prose. If the owner prefers suppression, suppress only in the narrow stdout summary (which is width-constrained anyway) while the artifact always carries the value, and never the reverse. Owner's call: this is the visibility-versus-false-mandate trade at the centre of the feature.

conflicts.quote: The literal `n/a` appears nowhere in the report or stdout; the only absence literals are the six in §3
conflicts.why: The closure rule is right and I want it; the enumeration is incomplete, and a closed vocabulary that is short is worse than an open one because the missing states must then be rendered as a literal that means something else. Two states both the architect and I require have no literal in the six. First, no-variation / degenerate: every eligible value in the cell is identical, so ranking is mathematically undefined — my R1 state table calls this out as 'must not be shown as 0.5, or no effect', and the architect's `CellState` carries `Degenerate { reason }` for it (also the no-positives / no-negatives case that `man_whitney_auc` returns as `None` today). `undefined (base rate 0.00)` covers only the no-positives cause. Second, no paired outcome for this horizon in a per-symbol group, which my AC-S3 requires be reported rather than the symbol being dropped — that is not `no input`, because the input was carried; the label was not.
conflicts.proposal: Extend the closed set from six to eight, keeping the closure rule and UX-6's scan intact: add a no-variation literal that names the cause and the n (values identical, ranking undefined) and a no-paired-outcome literal that names the horizon and the sample count. Exact wording is UX's; I need only that the two states exist as their own literals and that AC-D4 and AC-S3 have something legal to render.

conflicts.quote: The standing verdict is **derived from the run's window/sample counts**, not a constant: a run below the session bar renders `BELOW BAR`/`DEGENERATE`, a run meeting it does not
conflicts.why: Derivation is right, and the anti-wallpaper argument behind it is right. But the bar UX prints in §2 includes 'spanning >= M calendar weeks', and the architect's ring-cap arithmetic means one run's window can never exceed roughly seven sessions per symbol — under two calendar weeks — because the rows are evicted. So the clause 'a run meeting it does not' describes a branch that cannot be reached by construction, the verdict is a constant `BELOW BAR` forever, and UX-2 becomes the wallpaper it was written to prevent. The multi-week half of the bar is only evaluable across saved artifacts, which my scope explicitly future-dates and which is out of v1. I am not asking to raise retention here; I am asking that the output not print a bar it cannot ever measure as though it might.
conflicts.proposal: Split the bar in the standing block. The in-run verdict is derived only from what one run can measure — this slice's distinct-session count and its lift@top decile on `large_abs_move`. The multi-week half prints as an explicitly out-of-run condition with its own standing value (wording UX's, e.g. a 'cannot evaluate in one run — multi-week bar is cross-artifact' literal), so the operator reads an unmet-by-construction condition rather than a verdict. The numbers, which UX correctly says are mine and which my R1 left incomplete: reporting floor 30 rows per cell; in-run bar = lift@top decile >= 1.10 on `large_abs_move` with n_sessions >= 10; cross-artifact bar = that lift sustained across artifacts spanning >= 3 calendar weeks. I recommend these three numbers; the owner sets them, and the >= 10 sessions figure in particular is a judgment about how much autocorrelated evidence counts as evidence.

conflicts.quote: | UX-2 | The standing verdict is **derived from the run's window/sample counts**, not a constant: a run below the session bar renders `BELOW BAR`/`DEGENERATE`, a run meeting it does not | default, degenerate | **test** | Silently regresses to a hardcoded string under refactor; a constant hedge is the current failure |
conflicts.why: This is my own R1 criterion and PM is right to forbid it. PM's Out list rules out 'any adoption recommendation, "winner", "best signal", or per-run pass/fail against the runbook's multi-week bar', and AC-G4 scans the run's strings for exactly this. A standing verdict of `BELOW BAR` / `AT BAR` IS a per-run pass/fail against the multi-week bar, and the day it prints `AT BAR` the tool has issued the mandate `[score-change-is-deliberate-and-measured]` exists to prevent. My anti-wallpaper argument does not justify emitting a verdict the feature is forbidden to reach.
conflicts.proposal: Retract `BELOW BAR` / `AT BAR` from the standing vocabulary. Keep the standing block, keep it derived (so it does not become wallpaper), but derive the varying part from the architect's `evidence_class` — evidence-strength FACTS only: `SINGLE SESSION` · `MULTI-SESSION (d=3)` · `MULTI-WEEK (d=11)` · `DEGENERATE — single symbol` · `INSUFFICIENT — cannot evaluate`. The bar's own text may still be PRINTED verbatim beside the run's values (so the reader can do the comparison), but the tool never states the outcome of that comparison. UX-2 becomes: the standing line's evidence class is derived from `n_sessions` and the group set, never a constant, and contains no pass/fail token.

conflicts.quote: | Level geometry candidates | **Distance to flip (%)**, **Distance to wall (%)** | "level signal", "geometry score", "proximity edge" |
conflicts.why: My own approved-term row is wrong given the architect's verified finding that `dist_to_flip_pct` / `dist_to_wall_pct` are SIGNED and that the ranked scalar will be `-abs(signed value)`. A column headed 'Distance to flip (%)' over a folded absolute-value scalar renames what the value actually is — and the raw signed field ranks the FARTHEST rows at the top decile, so the same label would be false in two different directions depending on whether orientation was applied. My table also bans 'proximity', which is the only honest word for the oriented scalar.
conflicts.proposal: Replace the row with: approved term **Closeness to flip** / **Closeness to nearer wall**, rendered with its basis expression inline — `Closeness to flip (ranked on -|signed distance to flip, %|; higher = nearer)`. Un-ban 'proximity' (keep 'proximity edge' banned — 'edge' is the adoption word, not 'proximity'). Every geometry row must print both the raw field name and the fold, because 'we ranked the absolute distance' and 'we ranked the signed distance' are different findings that render identically without it. Add an AC: no geometry row's label may use the word 'distance' unqualified by its sign treatment (Verify by: test — a scan, since a later width-saving edit re-introduces it silently).

conflicts.quote: **Every cell is in exactly one of these states, and they are visually and textually distinct:**
conflicts.why: Three closed vocabularies now exist over the same cells — PM's five states, my six absence literals, and the architect's `CellState` (4) plus `Ineligible` (4) — and they do not map one-to-one. Shipping two of them puts two different words on the same state, which is the precise failure `[absent-is-not-none]` exists to prevent. Concretely, PM's set is declared exhaustive but has no state for a metric that does not exist for the pair (calibration on a boolean candidate) or for a block that was requested off (`--driver-loo`), so those get forced into 'no sample carried this input', which is a false claim. Symmetrically my six literals have no state for PM's 'no paired outcome', which AC-S3 requires; and PM's single 'no variation' covers the candidate being constant while the architect's `Degenerate { reason }` also has to cover the label being constant (no positives / no negatives) — a different fact with a different remedy.
conflicts.proposal: Adopt ONE vocabulary at three layers, agreed here and stated once in the SPEC: architect's `Ineligible` (per-row, why a sample left a candidate) → `CellState` (per-cell) → one rendering literal per `CellState`, owned by me. The `CellState` set must be the union: `Computed` · `Computed { under_powered: n, floor }` · `NoEligibleRows { by_reason }` · `NoPairedOutcome { n_samples }` · `DegenerateCandidate { constant_value }` · `DegenerateLabel { n_pos, n_neg }` · `NotApplicable` · `NotRun { flag }`. My six literals are re-issued as exactly one per variant, and UX-6's scan becomes: no string outside that literal set, and no `n/a`, blank, `null`, `NaN`, `-` or bare `0`, appears in any cell. If any lane adds a variant later it must add a literal in the same change.

conflicts.quote: Every cell carries `n_eligible` **and** an `excluded_by_reason` map keyed by the enum variant.
conflicts.why: A map keyed by the extractor's `Ineligible` variants can only explain rows that REACHED an extractor. A group with zero paired rows — PM's AC-S3, 'a symbol present in the slice whose samples produced no paired outcomes' — never calls an extractor, so `excluded_by_reason` is an EMPTY map and the cell renders with a count of nothing and no reason. That is the 2026-08-11 `n = 0` failure returning through the mechanism built to prevent it, one level up. The same hole swallows 'this metric does not exist for this candidate/label pair' and 'this block was switched off', neither of which is a per-row exclusion at all.
conflicts.proposal: Make the cell's reason a group-level disposition, not a derivative of the row-level map: every cell carries `state: CellState` (the union in my previous conflict) as a first-class field that is REQUIRED even when `excluded_by_reason` is empty, plus `n_paired_in_group` so `n_eligible + sum(excluded_by_reason) = n_paired_in_group` reconciles and a zero-row group is distinguishable from a fully-excluded one. Add an architect-side invariant test: no cell may carry `n_eligible == 0` with an empty `excluded_by_reason` AND a state that does not name a group-level cause.

conflicts.quote: | **AC-D5** | S4 | When no loaded sample carries a score-driver breakdown, the attribution section states that it was **not attempted** and gives the count of samples lacking it — it does not print rows of `n = 0`. | test |
conflicts.why: 'Not attempted' asserts something the run did not do. Attribution WAS attempted; every sample lacked the input. Those are two different facts with two different remedies for the reader (turn the flag on vs. wait for post-2026-08-10 captures to accumulate), and collapsing them is the same class of error as the `n = 0` cell this AC exists to kill. PM's own AC-D1 uses the correct words ('no sample carried this input') for the identical situation, so the AC set is internally inconsistent — and this is the sentence that will land in SPEC §3 and bind the copy.
conflicts.proposal: Restate AC-D5 as: the attribution section renders `no input (0 of N samples carried score_drivers)` — attempted, nothing eligible — and reserves `not run (--driver-loo off)` for the case where the block was switched off. Both counts named, neither word borrowed for the other. PM ceded exact wording to me (their Assumptions §UX/Tech-writer), so I read this as an inconsistency to fix rather than a scope fight — but it must be fixed before synthesis, because the AC text is the copy.

conflicts.quote: | **AC-C4** | S7 | Re-running the retained 2026-08-11 paired slice reproduces the deep dive's published figures to their published precision: composite AUC 0.467 and lift@top10 0.17, structure-event AUC 0.932, SPY Pearson +0.51, QQQ Pearson −0.31, SPY lift 1.43, QQQ lift 0.56. | test |
conflicts.why: The per-symbol half of that list is hand-derived — the deep dive's own table is labelled '(hand-paired)' — and this AC promotes hand-derived numbers to a test oracle, inverting the direction of vouching that the whole feature exists to establish.
